title: GitHub Commit Failure Rate
dataSources: GitHub repositories (`github:repo`), commits (`github:commit`), issues (`github:issue`), and releases (`github:release`).
app: GitHub repository metadata, commit activity feeds, issue trackers, and release publish logs forwarded to Splunk HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=github:commit
| eval status_value=lower(coalesce(commit_status,"unknown"))
| eval failed=if(match(status_value,"error|fail|alert|overdue|late|stale|breach"),1,0)
| stats count as events, sum(failed) as failed_events by repo_name
| eval failure_pct=round(100*failed_events/events,1)
| sort - failure_pct - failed_events
description: Measures how often GitHub commit records land in an unhealthy or exception state for each repository.
value: A plain failure-rate view highlights noisy devices, flaky automations, and habits that repeatedly slip.
implementation: Normalize commit_status values into good or bad states and review the failure percentage per repository.
visualization: Bar chart of failure percentage by entity.
grandmaExplanation: It highlights which parts of your GitHub commit data keep ending up in a bad state instead of working cleanly.
